questions.q: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Let $A = \mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}{\left(- 1\right)}^{k} \times Ck n \left[{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{k} + {\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)}^{k} + {\left(\dfrac{7}{8}\right)}^{k} + {\left(\dfrac{15}{16}\right)}^{k} + {\left(\dfrac{31}{32}\right)}^{k}\right]$. If $63A = 1 - \dfrac{1}{{2}^{30}},$ then $n$ is equal to ______ .<gwmw style="display:none;"></gwmw>
questions.solution:
$A = \mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n} Ck n \left[{\left(- \dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{k} + {\left(\dfrac{- 3}{4}\right)}^{k} + {\left(\dfrac{- 7}{8}\right)}^{k} + {\left(\dfrac{- 15}{16}\right)}^{k} + {\left(\dfrac{- 31}{32}\right)}^{k}\right]$

$A = {\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{n} + {\left(1 - \dfrac{3}{4}\right)}^{n} + {\left(1 - \dfrac{7}{8}\right)}^{n} + {\left(1 - \dfrac{15}{16}\right)}^{n} + {\left(1 - \dfrac{31}{32}\right)}^{n}$

$A = \dfrac{1}{{2}^{n}} + \dfrac{1}{{4}^{n}} + \dfrac{1}{{8}^{n}} + \dfrac{1}{{16}^{n}} + \dfrac{1}{{32}^{n}}$

$A = \dfrac{1}{{2}^{n}}\left(\dfrac{1 - {\left(\dfrac{1}{{2}^{n}}\right)}^{5}}{1 - \dfrac{1}{{2}^{n}}}\right) ⇒ A = \dfrac{\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{{2}^{5n}}\right)}{\left({2}^{n} - 1\right)}$

$\left({2}^{n} - 1\right)A = 1 - \dfrac{1}{{2}^{5n}},$

Given, $63A = 1 - \dfrac{1}{{2}^{30}}$

Clearly $5n = 30$

$n = 6$

questions.q: If $n$ is the number of irrational terms in the expansion of ${\left({3}^{1 / 4} + {5}^{1 / 8}\right)}^{60}$, then $\left(n - 1\right)$ is divisible by :
questions.solution:
${\left({3}^{1 / 4} + {5}^{1 / 8}\right)}^{60}$

$= Cr 60 {\left({3}^{1 / 4}\right)}^{60 - r} . {\left({5}^{1 / 8}\right)}^{r}$

$= Cr 60 \left(3\right)\dfrac{60 - r}{4} . 5\dfrac{r}{8}$

For rational terms.

$\dfrac{r}{8} = k; 0 \le r \le 60$

$0 \le 8k \le 60$

$0 \le k \le \dfrac{60}{8}$

$0 \le k \le 7 . 5$

$k = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7$

$\dfrac{60 - 8k}{4}$ is always divisible by $4$ for all value of $k$

Total rational terms $= 8$

Total terms $= 61$

irrational terms $= 53$

$n - 1 = 53 - 1 = 52$

$52$ is divisible by $26$.

questions.q: Let $m, n \in N$ and $gcd\left(2, n\right) = 1$. If $30\left(\begin{array}{ll}30 \\ 0\end{array}\right) + 29\left(\begin{array}{ll}30 \\ 1\end{array}\right) + \ldots . . + 2\left(\begin{array}{ll}30 \\ 28\end{array}\right) + 1\left(\begin{array}{ll}30 \\ 29\end{array}\right) = n . {2}^{m}$, then $n + m$ is equal to _______. (Here $\left(\begin{array}{ll}n \\ k\end{array}\right) = Ck n$)
questions.solution:
$30\left(C0 30\right) + 29\left(C1 30\right) + \ldots + 2\left(C28 30\right) + 1\left(C29 30\right)$

$= 30\left(C30 30\right) + 29\left(C29 30\right) + \ldots \ldots + 2\left(C2 30\right) + 1\left(C1 30\right)$

$= \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{30}r\left(Cr 30\right)$

$= \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{30}r\left(\dfrac{30}{r}\right)\left(Cr - 1 29\right)$

$= 30\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{30} Cr - 1 29$

$= 30\left(C0 29 + C1 29 + C2 29 + \ldots + C29 29\right)$

$= 30\left({2}^{29}\right) = 15{\left(2\right)}^{30} = n{\left(2\right)}^{m}$

$∴ n = 15, m = 30$

$n + m = 45$

questions.q: If $n ⩾ 2$ is a positive integer, then the sum of the series $C2 n + 1 + 2\left(C2 2 + C2 3 + C2 4 + \ldots + C2 n\right)$ is
questions.solution:
$C2 n + 1 + 2\left(C2 2 + C2 3 + C2 4 + \ldots + C2 n\right)$

$C2 n + 1 + 2\left(C3 3 + C2 3 + C2 4 + \ldots + C2 n\right)$

{use $Cr + 1 n + Cr n = Cr n + 1$}

$= C2 n + 1 + 2\left(C3 4 + C2 4 + C3 5 + \ldots + C2 n\right)$

$= C2 n + 1 + 2\left(C3 5 + C2 5 + \ldots + C2 n\right)$

$= C2 n + 1 + 2\left(C3 n + C2 n\right)$

$= C2 n + 1 + 2 \cdot C3 n + 1$

$= \dfrac{\left(n + 1\right)n}{2} + 2 \cdot \dfrac{\left(n + 1\right)\left(n\right)\left(n - 1\right)}{2 . 3}$

$= \dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)\left(2n + 1\right)}{6}$

questions.q: For integers $n$ and $r,$ let $\left(\begin{array}{ll}n \\ r\end{array}\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}Cr n , & ifn \ge r \ge 0 \\ 0, & otherwise\end{cases}\right$. The maximum value of $k$ for which the sum $\mathop{∑}_{i = 0}^{k}\left(\begin{array}{ll}10 \\ i\end{array}\right)\left(\begin{array}{ll}15 \\ k - i\end{array}\right) + \mathop{∑}_{i = 0}^{k + 1}\left(\begin{array}{ll}12 \\ i\end{array}\right)\left(\begin{array}{ll}13 \\ k + 1 - i\end{array}\right)$ is maximum, is equal to _________.
questions.solution:
$( 1 + x{)}^{10} = C0 10 + C1 10 x + C2 10 {x}^{2} + \ldots \ldots + C10 10 {x}^{10}$
$( 1 + x{)}^{15} = C0 15 + C1 15 x + \ldots . Ck - 1 15 {x}^{k - 1} + Ck 15 {x}^{k} + Ck + 1 15 {x}^{k + 1} + \ldots {\ldots}^{15}{C}_{15}{x}^{15}$
$\mathop{∑}_{i = 0}^{k}\left(\begin{array}{ll}10 \\ i\end{array}\right)\left(\begin{array}{ll}15 \\ k - i\end{array}\right) = C0 10 . Ck 15 + C1 10 . Ck - 1 15 + \ldots . + Ck 10 . C0 15$
Coefficient of ${x}^{k}$ in $( 1 + x{)}^{25}$
$= Ck 25$
$\mathop{∑}_{i = 0}^{k + 1}\left(\begin{array}{ll}12 \\ i\end{array}\right)\left(\begin{array}{ll}13 \\ k + 1 - i\end{array}\right) = \mathop{∑}_{i = 0}^{k + 1}\left(Ci 12\right)\left(Ck + 1 - i 13\right) =$C0 12 . Ck + 1 13 + C1 12 . Ck 13 + \ldots . . + Ck + 1 12 . C0 13$

Coefficient of ${x}^{k + 1}$ in $( 1 + x{)}^{25}$
$= Ck + 1 25$

$Ck 25 + Ck + 1 25 = Ck + 1 26$
For maximum value
$k + 1 = 13$
$k = 12$

as $Cr n$ is defined for all values of $n$ as well as $r$ so $Ck + 1 26$ always exists.

questions.q: The natural number $m$, for which the coefficient of $x$ in the binomial expansion of  ${\left({x}^{m} + \dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}}\right)}^{22}$ is 1540, is
questions.solution:
The general term in the binomial expansion,

${T}_{r + 1} = Cr 22 {\left({x}^{m}\right)}^{22 - r}{x}^{- 2r}$

$⇒ {T}_{r + 1} = Cr 22 {x}^{m ( 22 - r ) - 2r}$

For the coefficient of $x$

$22m - mr - 2r = 1$

$⇒ 22m - 1 = r ( m + 2 )$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{22m - 1}{m + 2}$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{22m + 44 - 45}{m + 2}$

$r = 22 - \dfrac{3 . 3 . 5}{m + 2} ⇒ 22 - r = \dfrac{3 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{m + 2}$

Since, $Cr 22 = C22 - r 22$

So possible values of $m = 1, 3, 7, 13, 43$, but $C3 22 = 1540 ⇒ 22 - r = 3 ⇒ m = 13$

questions.q: If for some positive integer $n$, the coefficients of three consecutive terms in the binomial expansion of ${\left(1 + x\right)}^{n + 5}$ are in the ratio $5: 10: 14$, then the largest coefficient in the expansion is :
questions.solution:
Let three consecutive terms are ${T}_{r}, {T}_{r + 1}, {T}_{r + 2}$
So, $\dfrac{Cr - 1 n + 5}{Cr n + 5} = \dfrac{5}{10}$ and $\dfrac{Cr n + 5}{Cr + 1 n + 5} = \dfrac{10}{14}$

Using property $\dfrac{Cr n}{Cr - 1 n} = \dfrac{n - r + 1}{r}$, we have

$\dfrac{\left(n + 5\right) - r + 1}{r} = 2$ and $\dfrac{\left(n + 5\right) - \left(r + 1\right) + 1}{r + 1} = \dfrac{7}{5}$

$⇒ n - 3r + 6 = 0$ and $5n - 12r + 18 = 0$

Solving both equations, $n = 6, r = 4$
Hence, the greatest coefficient will be of middle term, which is $= C5 n + 5 = C5 11 = 462$

questions.solution:
${\left(x + \sqrt{{x}^{2} - 1}\right)}^{6} + {\left(x - \sqrt{{x}^{2} - 1}\right)}^{6} = 2\left[{C}_{0}{x}^{6} + {C}_{2}{x}^{4}\left({x}^{2} - 1\right) + {C}_{4}{x}^{2}{\left({x}^{2} - 1\right)}^{2} + {C}_{6}{\left({x}^{2} - 1\right)}^{3}\right]$

$= 2\left[{x}^{6} + 15\left({x}^{6} - {x}^{4}\right) + 15{x}^{2}\left({x}^{4} - 2{x}^{2} + 1\right) + \left(- 1 + 3{x}^{2} - 3{x}^{4} + {x}^{6}\right)\right]$

$= 2\left(32{x}^{6} - 48{x}^{4} + 18{x}^{2} - 1\right)$

Now given that $\alpha \text{ and } \beta$ are the coefficients of ${x}^{4} \text{ and } {x}^{2}$ respectively, hence

$\alpha = - 96$ and $\beta = 36$

$∴ \alpha - \beta = - 132$

Let $\left(1 - x + {x}^{2} . .\right)\left(1 + x + {x}^{2} \ldots\right) = {a}_{0} + {a}_{1} \times {a}_{2}{x}^{2} + \ldots$

Put $x = - 1$

From \left(1\right) + \left(2\right)
$4n + 2 = 2 $\left({a}_{0} + {a}_{2} + \ldots\right)$
$= 2 \times 61$
$⇒ 2n + 1 = 61 ⇒ n = 30$

To find the coefficient of term independent of $x$ in given expression, first let's find constant term and coefficient of ${x}^{- 8}$ in the expansion of ${\left(2{x}^{2} - \dfrac{3}{{x}^{2}}\right)}^{6}$
${T}_{r + 1}{=}^{6}{C}_{r}{\left(2{x}^{2}\right)}^{6 - r} \times {\left(- \dfrac{3}{{x}^{2}}\right)}^{r}$
${T}_{r + 1}{=}^{6}{C}_{r}{2}^{6 - r} \times {\left(- 3\right)}^{r} \times {x}^{12 - 4r}$
For constant term: $r = 3$ , hence constant term = ${}^{6}{C}_{3}{2}^{3} \times {\left(- 3\right)}^{3} \times {x}^{0}$
For coefficient of ${x}^{- 8}: r = 5$ , hence coefficient of ${x}^{- 8}{=}^{6}{C}_{5} \times {2}^{1}{\left(- 3\right)}^{5} \times {x}^{- 8}$
Given expression can be written as
$\left(\dfrac{1}{60} - \dfrac{{x}^{8}}{81}\right)\left({}^{6}{C}_{3} \times {2}^{3} \times {\left(- 3\right)}^{3} \times {x}^{0} + \ldots + {}^{6}{C}_{5} \times {2}^{1} \times {\left(- 3\right)}^{5} \times {x}^{- 8} + \ldots\right)$
Hence, coefficient of term independent of $x$
$= \dfrac{1}{60}{\times}^{6}{C}_{3} \times {2}^{3}{\left(- 3\right)}^{3} - \dfrac{1}{81}{\times}^{6}{C}_{5} \times {2}^{1} \times {\left(- 3\right)}^{5}$
$= - 72 + 36 = - 36$

questions.q: The coefficient of ${x}^{18}$ in the product $\left(1 + x\right){\left(1 - x\right)}^{10}{\left(1 + x + {x}^{2}\right)}^{9}$ is
questions.solution:
$\left(1 + x\right){\left(1 - x\right)}^{10}{\left(1 + x + {x}^{2}\right)}^{9}$
$= \left(1 + x\right)\left(1 - x\right){\left(1 - x\right)}^{9}{\left(1 + x + {x}^{2}\right)}^{9}$
$= \left(1 - {x}^{2}\right){\left[\left(1 - x\right)\left(1 + x + {x}^{2}\right)\right]}^{9}$
$= \left(1 - {x}^{2}\right){\left(1 - {x}^{3}\right)}^{9}$
So, Coefficient of ${x}^{18} in \left(1 + x\right){\left(1 - x\right)}^{10}{\left(1 + x + {x}^{2}\right)}^{9}$
$=$ Coefficient of ${x}^{18} in \left(1 - {x}^{2}\right){\left(1 - {x}^{3}\right)}^{9}$
$=$Coefficient of ${x}^{18} in \left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)\left[{C}_{0} 9 + {C}_{1} 9 \left(- {x}^{3}\right) + {C}_{2}{\left(- {x}^{3}\right)}^{2} + \ldots 9\right]$
$= {C}_{6} 9 {\left(- 1\right)}^{6} = {C}_{3} 9 = \dfrac{9.8 . 7}{1.2 . 3} = 84$

questions.q: The smallest natural number $n$ , such that the coefficient of $x$ in the expansion of ${\left({x}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{{x}^{3}}\right)}^{n}$ is $C23 n$ , is
questions.solution:
In the expansion of ${\left({x}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{{x}^{3}}\right)}^{n}$ the general term is ${T}_{r + 1} = {C}_{r} n {\left({x}^{2}\right)}^{n - r}{\left(\dfrac{1}{{x}^{3}}\right)}^{r}$

$= {C}_{r} n {x}^{2n - 2r - 3r} = {C}_{r} n {x}^{2n - 5r}$

For coefficient of $x$, $2n - 5r = 1$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{2n - 1}{5}$

So, we have the coefficient as $C\dfrac{2n - 1}{5} n$

Using, the given value and $Cr n = Cn - r n$

$⇒ C\dfrac{2n - 1}{5} n = {C}_{23} = {C}_{n - 23} n n$

If $\dfrac{2n - 1}{5} = 23 ⇒ n = 58$ and if $\dfrac{2n - 1}{5} = n - 23 ⇒ n = 38$

Thus, the minimum value of $'n'$ is $38 .$

questions.q: If some three consecutive coefficients in the binomial expansion of ${\left(x + 1\right)}^{n}$ in powers of $x$ are in the ratio $2: 15: 70,$ then the average of these three coefficients is:
questions.solution:
From the given condition

${}^{n}{C}_{r}{:}^{n}{C}_{r + 1}{:}^{n}{C}_{r + 2} = 2: 15: 70$

$⇒ \dfrac{{}^{n}{C}_{r}}{{}^{n}{C}_{r + 1}} = \dfrac{2}{15}$ and $\dfrac{{}^{n}{C}_{r + 1}}{{}^{n}{C}_{r + 2}} = \dfrac{15}{70}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{n !}{\left(n - r\right) ! \cdot r !}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{n !}{\left(n - r - 1\right) ! \cdot \left(r + 1\right) !}\right)} = \dfrac{2}{15}$ and $\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{n !}{\left(n - r - 1\right) ! \cdot \left(r + 1\right) !}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{n !}{\left(n - r - 2\right) ! \cdot \left(r + 2\right) !}\right)} = \dfrac{15}{70}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(n - r - 1\right) ! \cdot \left(r + 1\right) !}{\left(n - r\right) ! \cdot r !} = \dfrac{2}{15}$ and $\dfrac{\left(n - r - 2\right) ! \cdot \left(r + 2\right) !}{\left(n - r - 1\right) ! \cdot \left(r + 1\right) !} = \dfrac{3}{14}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(n - r - 1\right) ! \cdot \left(r + 1\right) \cdot r !}{\left(n - r\right) \cdot \left(n - r - 1\right) ! \cdot r !} = \dfrac{2}{15}$ and $\dfrac{\left(n - r - 2\right) ! \cdot \left(r + 2\right) \cdot \left(r + 1\right) !}{\left(n - r - 1\right) \cdot \left(n - r - 2\right) ! \cdot \left(r + 1\right) !} = \dfrac{3}{14}$

$⇒ \dfrac{r + 1}{n - r} = \dfrac{2}{15}$ and $\dfrac{r + 2}{n - r - 1} = \dfrac{3}{14}$

$⇒ 17r = 2n - 15$ and $17r = 3n - 31$

$⇒ 3n - 31 = 2n - 15, ⇒ n = 16$ and $r = 1$

Hence, average $= \dfrac{{}^{n}{C}_{r}{+}^{n}{C}_{r + 1}{+}^{n}{C}_{r + 2}}{3}$

$= \dfrac{{}^{16}{C}_{1}{+}^{16}{C}_{2}{+}^{16}{C}_{3}}{3}$

$= 232 .$

questions.q: If the fourth term in the Binomial expansion of ${\left(\dfrac{2}{x} + {x}^{{\log}_{8}x}\right)}^{6}, \left(x > 0\right)$ is $20 \times {8}^{7},$ then a value of $x$ is
questions.solution:
The general term in the binomial expansion ${\left(a + b\right)}^{n}$ is ${T}_{r + 1} = Cr n {a}^{n - r}{b}^{r} .$

Given, the fourth term in the expansion of ${\left(\dfrac{2}{x} + {x}^{{\log}_{8}x}\right)}^{6}$ is

${T}_{4} = 20 \times {8}^{7}$

$⇒ C3 6 {\left(\dfrac{2}{x}\right)}^{3}{\left({x}^{{\log}_{8}x}\right)}^{3} = 20 \times {8}^{7}$

$⇒ \dfrac{6 !}{3 ! \cdot 3 !}{\left(\dfrac{2}{x}\right)}^{3}{\left({x}^{{\log}_{8}x}\right)}^{3} = 20 \times {\left({2}^{3}\right)}^{7}$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{6 \times 5 \times 4 \times 3 !}{3 \times 2 \times 1 \cdot 3 !}\right){\left(\dfrac{2}{x}\right)}^{3}{\left({x}^{{\log}_{8}x}\right)}^{3} = 20 \times {2}^{21}$

$⇒ \left(20\right){\left(\dfrac{2}{x}\right)}^{3}{\left({x}^{{\log}_{8}x}\right)}^{3} = 20 \times {2}^{21}$

$⇒ {\left[\left(\dfrac{2}{x}\right)\left({x}^{{\log}_{8}x}\right)\right]}^{3} = {\left({2}^{7}\right)}^{3}$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{2}{x}\right)\left({x}^{{\log}_{8}x}\right) = {2}^{7}$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)\left({x}^{{\log}_{8}x}\right) = {2}^{6}$

$⇒ {x}^{{\log}_{8}x - 1} = {8}^{2}$

Taking $log$ both side to the base $8$

$⇒ {\log}_{8}\left({x}^{{\log}_{8}x - 1}\right) = {\log}_{8}\left({8}^{2}\right)$

Using ${\log}_{a}{m}^{n} = n{\log}_{a}m,$ we get

$⇒ ( {\log}_{8}x - 1 )\left({\log}_{8}x\right) = 2$

$⇒ \left(t - 1\right)\left(t\right) = 2$ (Let ${\log}_{8}\left(x\right) = t$)

$⇒ {t}^{2} - t - 2 = 0$

$⇒ t = 2$ or $- 1$

$⇒ {\log}_{8}x = 2$ or $- 1$

If ${\log}_{a}x = b, ⇒ x = {a}^{b},$

$⇒ x = {8}^{2}$ or ${8}^{- 1}$

$⇒ x = 64$ or $\dfrac{1}{8} .$

questions.q: If the fourth term in the binomial expansion of ${\left(\sqrt{{x}^{\dfrac{1}{1 + {\log}_{10}x}}} + {x}^{\dfrac{1}{12}}\right)}^{6}$ is equal to $200,$ and $x > 1,$ then the value of $x$ is
questions.solution:
General term for the given binomial is
${T}_{r + 1} = {}^{6}{C}_{r}{\left(\sqrt{{x}^{\dfrac{1}{1 + {\log}_{10}x}}}\right)}^{6 - r}{\left({x}^{\dfrac{1}{12}}\right)}^{r}$
Given ${T}_{4} = 200,$ putting $r = 3$
$⇒ {T}_{4} = {}^{6}{C}_{3}{\left(\sqrt{{x}^{\dfrac{1}{1 + {\log}_{10}x}}}\right)}^{3}{\left({x}^{\dfrac{1}{12}}\right)}^{3} = 200$
$⇒ {\left({x}^{\dfrac{1}{1 + {\log}_{10}x}}\right)}^{\dfrac{3}{2}} ⋅ \left({x}^{\dfrac{1}{4}}\right) = 10$
$⇒ {x}^{\dfrac{3}{2\left(1 + {\log}_{10}x\right)} + \dfrac{1}{4}} = 10$
$⇒ \left(\dfrac{3}{2\left(1 + {\log}_{10}x\right)} + \dfrac{1}{4}\right){\log}_{10}x = 1$
$⇒ x = 10, {10}^{- 4}$
$⇒ x = 10$($ as $x > 1 )$

questions.q: If $n{C}_{4}, {}^{n}{C}_{5}$ and $n{C}_{6}$ are in A.P., then $n$ can be
questions.solution:
Since, $n{C}_{4}, {}^{n}{C}_{5}, {}^{n}{C}_{6}$ are in A.P.

$⇒ 2{\times}^{n}{C}_{5}{=}^{n}{C}_{4}{+}^{n}{C}_{6}$

$⇒ 2 \times \dfrac{n !}{5 ! \left(n - 5\right) !} = \dfrac{n !}{4 ! \left(n - 4\right) !} + \dfrac{n !}{6 ! \left(n - 6\right) !}$

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{5 ! \left(n - 5\right) !} = \dfrac{30 + \left(n - 5\right)\left(n - 4\right)}{6 ! \left(n - 4\right) !}$

$⇒ {n}^{2} - 21n + 98 = 0$

$⇒ n = 7$ or $14$

questions.q: The total number of irrational terms in the binomial expansion of ${\left(7\dfrac{1}{5} - 3\dfrac{1}{10}\right)}^{60}$ is
questions.solution:
General term is ${}^{60}{C}_{r}{\left({7}^{\dfrac{1}{5}}\right)}^{60 - r}{\left(- {3}^{\dfrac{1}{10}}\right)}^{r}$

We will get rational term when $r$ is multiple of $10$ and $60 - r$ is multiple of $5$.

$∴ r = 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60$

$∴$Number of irrational term $=$ Total terms $-$ Number of rational terms

$= \left(60 + 1\right) - 7 = 54$.

questions.solution:
Total number of terms in the expansion of ${\left(2\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{2\left(3\right)\dfrac{1}{3}}\right)}^{10} = 10 + 1 = 11$

questions.solution:
Given:

$\mathop{∑}_{r = 0}^{25}\left\{\left(Cr 50\right)\left(C25 - r 50 - r\right)\right\} = K\left(C25 50\right)$

$LHS$

$= \mathop{∑}_{r = 0}^{25}{}^{50}{C}_{r}{}^{50 - r}{C}_{25 - r}$

$= \mathop{∑}_{r = 0}^{25}\left[\left\{\dfrac{50 !}{r ! \left(50 - r\right) !}\right\}\left\{\dfrac{\left(50 - r\right) !}{\left(25 - r\right) ! \left(25\right) !}\right\}\right]$

$= {}^{50}{C}_{25}\mathop{∑}_{r = 0}^{25}{}^{25}{C}_{r}$

$= {}^{50}{C}_{25} \times {2}^{25}$

$= K\left(C25 50\right)$

$∴ K = {2}^{25}$

questions.q: The positive value of $\lambda$ for which the co-efficient of ${x}^{2}$ in the expansion ${x}^{2}{\left(\sqrt{x} + \dfrac{\lambda}{{x}^{2}}\right)}^{10}$ is $720,$ is
questions.solution:
Coefficient of ${x}^{2}$ in ${x}^{2}{\left(\sqrt{x} + \dfrac{\lambda}{{x}^{2}}\right)}^{10}$

$=$ coefficient of ${x}^{0}$ in ${\left(\sqrt{x} + \dfrac{\lambda}{{x}^{2}}\right)}^{10}$

A general term in the expansion ${\left(\sqrt{x} + \dfrac{\lambda}{{x}^{2}}\right)}^{10}$ is $10{C}_{r}{\left(\sqrt{x}\right)}^{10 - r}{\left(\dfrac{\lambda}{{x}^{2}}\right)}^{r}{=}^{10}{C}_{r}{\left(\lambda\right)}^{r}{\left(x\right)}^{5 - 5\dfrac{r}{2}}$

$⇒$ coefficient of ${x}^{0} = {}^{10}{C}_{2}{\lambda}^{2}$ (for $r = 2$ )

$= 45{\lambda}^{2}$

Now $45{\lambda}^{2} = 720$

$⇒ \lambda = \pm 4$

questions.q: If the third term in the binomial expansion of ${\left(1 + {x}^{{\log}_{2}x}\right)}^{5}$ equals $2560,$ then a possible value of $x$ is
questions.solution:
The general term in the expansion of ${\left(a + b\right)}^{n}$ is ${T}_{r + 1} = Cr n {a}^{n - r}{b}^{r} .$

Given, in the expansion of ${\left(1 + {x}^{{\log}_{2}x}\right)}^{5},$ third term is $2560$

$⇒ {T}_{3} = {}^{5}{C}_{2}{\left({x}^{{\log}_{2}x}\right)}^{2} = 2560$

Using, $Cr n = \dfrac{n !}{r ! \cdot \left(n - r\right) !},$ we get

$⇒ \dfrac{5 !}{2 ! \cdot 3 !}{\left({x}^{{\log}_{2}x}\right)}^{2} = 2560$

$⇒ \dfrac{5 \cdot 4 \cdot 3 !}{2 \times 1 \cdot 3 !}\left({x}^{2{\log}_{2}x}\right) = 2560$

$⇒ \left({x}^{2{\log}_{2}x}\right) = 256$

Taking logarithm to the base $2$ on both sides

$⇒ {\log}_{2}\left({x}^{2{\log}_{2}x}\right) = {\log}_{2}256$

Now, using ${\log}_{a}{m}^{n} = n{\log}_{a}m \text{ and } {\log}_{a}a = 1,$

$⇒ 2lo{g}_{2}x\left({\log}_{2}x\right) = {\log}_{2}{2}^{8}$

$⇒ 2{\left({\log}_{2}x\right)}^{2} = 8$

$⇒ \left({\log}_{2}x\right) = \pm 2$

Using, ${\log}_{a}x = b, ⇒ x = {a}^{b}$

$x = {2}^{2}, {2}^{- 2}$

$⇒ x = 4, \dfrac{1}{4}$

Here, only $x = \dfrac{1}{4}$ is given in the options.

$\because(1+x)^2=1+2 x+x^2$,

Corresponding coefficients are $2 \times 4,2 \times 1 \times4,1 \times 3 \times 6,3 \times 6$ or 8,8,18,18.

8+8+18+18=52

Therefore, the coefficient of $x^{10}$ in the expansion of $(1+x)^2$\left(1+x^2\right)^3\left(1+x^3\right)^4$ is 52 .

questions.q: The sum $\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{10}\left({r}^{2} + 1\right) \times \left(r !\right)$, is equal to:
questions.solution:
$\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{10}\left({r}^{2} + 1\right)r !$
Let us express the ${r}^{th}$ term, as a difference involving consecutive factorials, ${T}_{r} = \left({r}^{2} + 1 + r - r\right)r ! = \left({r}^{2} + r\right)r ! - \left(r - 1\right)r !$
Therefore,
$⇒ {T}_{r} = r\left(r + 1\right) ! - \left(r - 1\right)r !$
Putting $r = 1, 2, 3, . . . , 10$and adding, we get $\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{10}\left\{r\left(r + 1\right) ! - \left(r - 1\right)r !\right\} = 10 \times 11 !$
$∴ \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{10}\left({r}^{2} + 1\right) \times r ! = 10 \times 11 !$

questions.solution:
Let coefficient of first term is $Cr n$

$\dfrac{Cr n}{Cr + 1 n} = \dfrac{1}{7}$

$⇒ \dfrac{r + 1}{n - r} = \dfrac{1}{7}$

$⇒ 7r + 7 = n - r$

$n - 8r = 7 \ldots \left(1\right)

Also, \dfrac{Cr + 1 n}{Cr + 2 n} = \dfrac{7}{42} = \dfrac{1}{6}

$⇒ $\dfrac{r + 2}{n - r - 1} = \dfrac{1}{6}

$⇒ 6r + 12 = n - r - 1$

$n - 7r = 13 \ldots $\left(2\right)$

Solving $\left(1\right)$ and $\left(2\right)$, we get $r = 6$

Hence, ${7}^{th}$ term is the answer.

questions.q: For natural numbers $m, n$ if $(1-y)^m(1+y)^n=1+a_1 y+a_2 y^2+\ldots$, and $a_1=a_2=10$ then $(\mathrm{m}, \mathrm{n})$ is
questions.solution:
$(1-y)^m(1+y)^n=\left[1-{ }^m C_1 y+{ }^m C_2 y^2-\ldots\right]\left[1+{ }^n C_1 y+{ }^n C_2 y^2+\ldots\right]=1+(n-m)+\left\{\frac{m(m-1)}{2}+\frac{n(n-1)}{2}-m n\right\} y^2+\ldots .$.
$\therefore a_1=n-m=10$ and $a_2=\frac{m^2+n-m-n-2 m n}{2}=10$
So, $n-m=10$ and $(m-n)^2-(m+n)=20 \quad \Rightarrow m+n=80$
\therefore $\mathrm{m}=$35, \quad $\mathrm{n}=$45
